newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia concerned over Israeli settlement policy.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia concerned over Israeli settlement policy.

text.p: Tunisian President Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali said on Thursday Israel was violating peace agreements with the Palestinians by building a controversial Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

"We reiterate our great concern for the future of the Middle East peace process threatened by a relapse given Israel's persistence in violating peace accords and their principles, and at first the principle of land-for-peace," Ben Ali said.
Addressing a speech marking Independence Day, the Tunisian president said the peace process was threatened by Israel's "obstinacy in pursuing settlements policy in Jerusalem and other regions."
He reiterated Tunisia's support for an independent Palestinian state "with Jerusalem as its capital" and the claim of Syria and Lebanon to regain lands occupied by Israel.

Ben Ali's comments echoed those of other Arab leaders and international condemnation after Israel this week started building a settlement on land between Jerusalem and Bethlehem, an area occupied by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war.
Palestinians say the construction precludes planned peace talks on the city's status.

Tunisia and Israel last year formally established low-level diplomatic relations by opening "interests bureaux" in Tunis and Tel Aviv, in parallel to the opening of a Tunisian mission in the Palestinian self-ruled Gaza Strip.
But Tunisia froze its ties with Israel in December following Israel's footdragging in implementing peace accords with the Palestinians that were due then and over its settlement policy.
